note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, after 8a340e018a). RFC 4760 Section 7: "If a BGP speaker receives from a neighbor an UPDATE message that contains the MP_REACH_NLRI or MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute, and if the speaker determines that the attribute is incorrect, the speaker MUST delete all the BGP routes received from that neighbor whose AFI/SAFI is the same as the one carried in the incorrect MP_REACH_NLRI or MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute." The only changed unit is TestRFC4760IncorrectMPReachDeletesTheNeighborsRoutes, and only its claim: it now names rfc7606ResetNotification instead of rfc7606SessionReset. Read session_validation.go: applyRFC7606 sends a result carrying a Notification straight to rfc7606ResetNotification, and rfc7606SessionReset itself only builds a 3/1 Notification and delegates to rfc7606ResetNotification, so the reworded claim is true on every reset path and claims nothing the body does not assert. The body is unchanged: an IPv4 MP_REACH whose /24 overruns by one octet (prefix length legal, so only the overrun can fire) through a real Established session must give an error, Idle, zero plugin callbacks and a NOTIFICATION with code 3; it does not pin the subcode, and the claim does not claim one. A discrimination record (rfc7606ResetNotification panicked, observed red) backs question 2 for this tag. The other units (message-level exact SessionReset + 3/9 for next-hop and MP_UNREACH length; the correct-MP_REACH negative; the rib and reactor peer-down deletion units) are unchanged and still carry the deletion half: Idle raises the peer-down that clears the neighbor's routes, a superset of the offending AFI/SAFI. Ran the reactor TestRFC4760IncorrectMP*/CorrectMP* units green. Verdict stands.
